To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

clathrin‐associated coated vesicles (CV) from rat skeletal muscle contain a high proportion of asymmetric acetylcholinestease (AChEs) isoforms, and that such a distribution is developmentally regulated, being higher in the neonate than in adult muscle.
(i) AChE iso­forms in muscle CVs differ in their sensitivity to alkaline extraction and (ii) muscle CVs contain a higher proportion of asymmetric AChE iso–forms in neonates compared to adult animals.

the main molecular forms of acetycholinesterase found in coated vesicles of rat skeletal muscles are asymmetric forms, especially A12, and that these vesicles may be destined for externalization at the neuromuscular junction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and functional significance of the AChEs present in rat muscle CV preparations.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the distribution and activity of AChE in skeletal muscle and with the role of CVs in this process.
the mechanisms involved in AChE externalization in rat skeletal muscles and the possible role that muscle CVs may play in such an externalization process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CV‐enrichment of AChE in the muscle is a function of both the developmental state of the muscle and the isoenzyme form of AChE.
AChE is a component of muscle CVs, but the precise function of such a vesicular association remains to be elucidated.
A‐forms are preferentially associated with the clathrin coat, while G‐forms are not, but that the association of A‐forms with clathrin is pH sensitive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CVs are involved in the delivery of AChE to the plasmalemmal surface of skeletal muscle cells, and that the relative proportions (G‐forms/A‐forms) of AChE associated with CVs are dependent upon the extent of muscle maturation.
the A‐forms are the major AChE species associated with muscle CVs.
the A‐forms are the major AChE iso-forms associated with CVs in developing and adult skeletal muscle, while the G‐forms are the predominant species in the plasmalemmal AChE fraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AChE‐containing CVs are present in both developing and adult skeletal muscles.
the relative proportions and the distribution of AChE molecular forms in rat muscle CV preparations depend on the extent of muscle maturation.

CV‐associated AChE may be involved in the externalization (and thus in the turnover) of the asymmetric AChE isoenzyme A12, which is known to be the predominant isoform in the adult neuromuscular synapse.
